facts.text: The cob_simulation metapackage describes itself as packages to work with the Care-O-bot within simulation environments such as Gazebo.
The cob_simulation metapackage depends on cob_bringup_sim, cob_gazebo, cob_gazebo_objects, cob_gazebo_tools and cob_gazebo_worlds.
The world launch includes gazebo_ros/empty_world.launch with the world_name, paused, use_sim_time and gui arguments.
The robot launch runs the gazebo_ros spawn_model node with -urdf -param robot_description and -model robot.
spawn_object.py waits for /gazebo/get_world_properties and creates a GetWorldProperties ServiceProxy on that absolute name.
spawn_object.py reads world_properties.model_names only when world_properties.success is true, and otherwise uses an empty model list.
move_object.py creates a GetModelState ServiceProxy on /gazebo/get_model_state and a SetModelState ServiceProxy and ModelState publisher on /gazebo/set_model_state.
move_object.py's get_model_state sends a request with only model_name set and returns the GetModelState response.
move_object.py's start-up loop calls get_model_state for its model and keeps waiting while the response's success is false.
move_object.py builds a ModelState with model_name, a Pose whose position is x/y and whose orientation is a yaw quaternion, and reference_frame 'world', then publishes it.
move_object.py sets reference_frame to 'world' for its ModelState messages.
move_object.py documents polygon points as forming a polygon in [m] and the initialpose argument as a Cartesian Pose.
remove_object.py creates a gazebo/delete_model ServiceProxy, waits for the absolute /gazebo/delete_model service, and calls it with the model name.
spawn_object.py assembles its spawn endpoint at runtime as '/gazebo/spawn_' + model_type + '_model'; the clone has no fixed spawn endpoint literal.
The clone's CI workflow builds for the single ROS distro noetic.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper adds libgazebo_ros_api_plugin to the server's plugins unless the arguments already name it.
empty_world.launch starts the Gazebo server as the node named gazebo of package gazebo_ros, with the physics engine argument -e $(arg physics).
empty_world.launch defaults its physics argument to ode.
empty_world.launch defaults its gui argument to true.
When gui is true, empty_world.launch starts the node gazebo_gui of type gzclient.
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service unpause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
gazeboQueueThread serves gazebo_queue_ in a loop with a 0.001 s wall-clock wait while the node handle is ok.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.
Among the world-update begin hooks that its comment says apply forces and publish sim time on /clock, the API plugin connects publishSimTime.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.
The API plugin advertises the set_model_state service on gazebo_queue_, the queue the pause uses.
The API plugin subscribes to the set_model_state topic on gazebo_queue_ with updateModelState as the callback.
updateModelState passes the received ModelState to setModelState.
setModelState records whether the world is paused, pauses it, sets the model pose, then restores the recorded paused state.
deleteModel publishes an entity_delete request, then loops, sleeping 1 ms per round, until the model is gone or ROS time passes its 60 s timeout.

determinism.notes: Event-driven recording fake with no physics step, collision or wall-clock pacing

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it answers the declared get_world_properties, get_model_state, delete_model and set_model_state endpoints and runs no Gazebo physics, controllers, sensors or object dynamics
the model list and robot pose in the fake are placeholders; a live run must receive them from the operator's Gazebo instance

the /gazebo/* service and topic implementations are in gazebo_ros, outside the pinned clone; the clone proves the client endpoint names and types; only the stop, its read-back and the facts cite gazebo_ros itself (the companion source)
spawn_object.py's spawn service is assembled at runtime from the model type, so no fixed spawn endpoint is declared or exercised; model spawning is NOT COVERED

the fake answers a delete of an absent model with success, while gazebo_ros 2.9.3 answers success false with 'DeleteModel: model does not exist' (companion api plugin 824-830), so a live delete of an absent model is a failed receipt

the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause (the pinned clone declares no pause, unpause, reset or stop service): the fake keeps a paused flag that /gazebo/pause_physics sets and /gazebo/get_physics_properties reports, and it does not serve /gazebo/unpause_physics; it runs no Gazebo World::Step, and its GetPhysicsProperties numbers are placeholders

a paused world still applies world edits: set_model_state teleports the model and restores the recorded paused state, and delete requests are processed on every step; the latch refuses this driver's edits until the reset, but other clients and the Gazebo GUI can edit, step or unpause the world at any time, and MHS does not watch the flag after the e-stop

the pause runs on the gazebo_ros callback queue one request at a time (gazeboQueueThread), so a spawn or delete still waiting for its world edit delays it; the e-stop then exceeds its 500 ms timeout and stays unconfirmed with the latch held and a background retry

the read-back needs the ODE engine (empty_world.launch's default): with another engine get_physics_properties returns false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held; a graph without gazebo_ros has neither service

the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 2.9.3 (Noetic) and 11 releases the companion citations name, and the clone's README table names only older distros; the CI line (Noetic) is the profile served, and a Melodic or Kinetic deployment is out of profile

no unpause is offered (SAFE-042): this package publishes no controller command. robot.launch includes cob_bringup, an exec_depend that is not in this clone (cob_gazebo/package.xml:18, robot.launch:12), and the component test addresses JointTrajectory topics /<component>_controller/command (component_test.py:78-81). The world launches spawn controllers this package does not command: position controllers in ipa-apartment.xml:13-14 and velocity controllers in ipa-kitchen.xml:14 and automotive-assembly-line.xml:15. elevator.py:64-66 publishes Float64 0, the close position, after the open position 0.87 (lines 51-55); that close publish moves the door, so it cannot clear a stored command. Those commands act again when the world runs. After mhs.safety.reset the world stays paused; the operator stops those controller nodes outside MHS, then unpauses with the Gazebo GUI (world.launch:14, gui defaults true) or rosservice call /gazebo/unpause_physics
the set_model_state command is a topic publication, so the receipt is transmission evidence only and does not prove that Gazebo applied the pose
the fixed get_model_state read names the model robot from the robot launch; a deployment that renames the spawned model must not use that read
both service reads require the response's success flag, so a GetModelState reply for a model that does not exist is refused instead of being returned as a default zero pose

measures.description: Pose of the model named robot in the Gazebo world frame
measures.name: robot_pose

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused and get_physics_properties read pause true back; the paused flag, not a measured standstill. No unpause is offered: controllers this package does not command keep their last command (robot.launch:12, ipa-apartment.xml:13-14). The Gazebo GUI or another client can unpause or step the world (a step advances it). World edits still act while paused. After mhs.safety.reset the world stays paused; the operator stops those nodes, then unpauses outside MHS (world.launch:14).
